identity.basisReason: Ketchup is a packaged processed food, so the prepared state in which it is sold and eaten is the canonical per-100g comparison identity.

scoreReadiness.summary: Complete generic ketchup profile with exact USDA nutrients and amino acids plus clearly labelled starch, GI, and digestibility working values.
caveats: Protein digestibility is a documented category estimate, not an exact ketchup measurement.
Glycemic index is a contextual estimate and varies with brand formulation and serving context.
Sugar, sodium, tomato concentration, and micronutrients vary across brands.

sourceNotes: Production-safe generic packaged ketchup entry scored as sold per 100g.
USDA SR Legacy FDC 168556 supplies the canonical catsup nutrient and amino-acid profile.
The 78% protein-digestibility value is a documented vegetable-category estimate; it describes the tiny protein amount and does not make ketchup a protein food.
Brand recipes vary materially in sugar, sodium, and tomato concentration, so this is a generic baseline rather than a claim about every bottle.

topPros.explanation: It is widely available, needs no preparation, and works as a quick condiment for everyday foods.

topCons.explanation: The USDA record contains 907 milligrams of sodium per 100g, a material tradeoff outside the visible mineral rows.

topCons.title: acidity can bother reflux
topCons.explanation: Tomato and vinegar make ketchup a rough fit for some people whose reflux is triggered by acidic foods.

topCons.explanation: A freehand squirt is easy to underestimate when it is spread across several parts of a meal.

closing.summary: Best bits are the lycopene angle, strong flavour, convenience, and some value as a lighter swap for creamy sauces. Weak spots are the sugar-heavy carb profile, almost no fibre or protein, weak vitamins and minerals, plus the sodium and reflux tradeoffs. Best for occasional low-calorie flavour rather than nutrition. Essentially, ketchup takes tomatoes, concentrates the flavour, then adds enough baggage that the useful tomato story cannot save the score.

scenes.narrationText: The upsides first: processed tomato brings a lycopene angle. The USDA record contains about 12 milligrams of lycopene per 100 grams, and processing tomato can make that carotenoid easier to absorb. Strong flavour can replace richer sauces. A little sweetness, acidity, and tomato umami can make a meal more appealing without needing a heavy creamy sauce. Cheap, familiar, and easy to use. It is widely available, needs no preparation, and works as a quick condiment for plenty of everyday foods.
